attributes.cardDescription: A time-off request with type, inclusive date range, and a reusable approval chain — the request/approval record, not a time-tracking ledger
attributes.readMe:
# PTO Request

## Summary
One employee's request for time off: who, which days, what type (vacation | sick | personal | parental | unpaid), why, and where the sign-off stands. The FOURTH real consumer of ApprovalChainField (after Position, Offer, and JobRequisition) — the chain is reused UNCHANGED, same step/decision model, same read-only stepper.

## Fields
- `employee` (linksTo Employee) — who is requesting time off.
- `ptoType` (PtoTypeField enum) — vacation | sick | personal | parental | unpaid. Colored via PTO_TYPE_COLORS (utils' stateColor pairs, no literal hex).
- `startDate`, `endDate` (DateField) — first and last day off, inclusive.
- `reason` (TextAreaField) — free-text context for approvers.
- `approvalChain` (contains ApprovalChainField) — reused unchanged from approval-chain-field.gts. Typically manager then HR.
- `requestedDate` (DateField) — when the request was raised.
- `days` (computed NumberField) — INCLUSIVE day count (endDate − startDate + 1). Undefined (not 0) when either bound is missing or the range is inverted — "no dates yet" is a different fact from "zero days".
- `status` (computed StringField) — mirrors the chain: draft (chain empty, not yet submitted) | in-progress | approved | rejected.
- `employeeName` (computed StringField) — DENORMALIZED copy of employee.name. Why: the fitted format is served as prerendered HTML and prerendered fitted does not resolve linksTo, so the tile reads this own-attribute. Same rationale as OnboardingChecklist.personName.
- `title` (computed) — "{employeeName} — {ptoType}, {days}d", degrading gracefully when parts are missing.
- `cardTitle` (computed) — `cardInfo.name || title`, so a user's rename wins in the operator-mode stack header.

## Import
```ts
import { PtoRequest } from './pto-request';
```

## Formats
**Isolated:** header with the person, type pill, and status pill; main panel puts the date range and inclusive day count front and center, then the reason, then the approval chain panel (`<@fields.approvalChain />`, the read-only stepper with bottleneck badges).

**Embedded:** name + compact date range with day count + type pill + status pill.

**Fitted:** four tiers, each ADDING fields — ≤50px: employeeName + type pill; >50px: + day count; >80px: + date range; >130px: + status and "N of M" sign-off progress. Attribute-only: reads employeeName/days/status, never the employee link. 11px floor.

**Atom:** name + type pill.

**Edit:** default field editor — same convention as JobRequisition/Offer/Position (linksTo chooser for employee, enum dropdown for type, date pickers, and the chain's own containsMany editor).

## Usage — three ways this is used

**1. Employee self-service request.** An employee creates the card, picks dates and a type, writes the reason, and submits by adding the approval chain steps (manager, then HR). The `days` computed keeps the inclusive count honest.

**2. Manager approval queue via the tracker.** The Talent & Resource Tracker lists PtoRequests with a live query (no linksToMany anywhere), filtered to `status: in-progress` — the ApprovalChainField's bottleneck badge surfaces requests stuck on one desk.

**3. Capacity view on Projects.** Approved requests overlapping a project's window tell a staffing plan who is actually available — the app-side query joins approved PtoRequest date ranges against project timelines.

Balance math belongs to the app: `Employee.ptoAllowanceDays` (days/year) minus the sum of approved request `days` is computed via a live query over these cards — deliberately NOT a linksToMany on Employee, so requests never need manual attaching.

## Boundary (non-goals)
This is the REQUEST/APPROVAL record, not a time-tracking ledger. No accrual schedules, no half-day granularity, no carry-over rules, no calendar-sync — those belong to a payroll/time system. One card = one contiguous absence.

## Reuse notes
- Reuses **ApprovalChainField** (approval-chain-field.gts) unchanged — fourth consumer.
- Status/type colors flow through utils' `stateColor`/`stateColorOf` token pairs.

## Examples
- `PtoRequest/priya-vacation-approved` — 5-day vacation, two-step chain fully approved.
- `PtoRequest/leo-personal-pending` — 3-day personal request, manager approved, HR step pending (mid-chain).
- `PtoRequest/dana-vacation-draft` — year-end vacation with an EMPTY chain, demonstrating the `draft` status.
